title: Calcite preserves bag multiplicity across projected set operations
summary: The same planner hook as the upstream SQL fixture enabled the transpose rule on JDBC. EXCEPT and INTERSECT now compare the full rows. Changing only the right bag changed the fixed counts from 2/1 to 0/3.

change.description: The planner limits projection pushdown across EXCEPT ALL and INTERSECT ALL to permutations that preserve every input field.

notes: The JDBC caller also ran with a public planner listener on both pins. Field trimming removed the outer projection over UNION ALL before optimization. Other optimizer rules fired, the transpose rule received zero attempts, and both tens survived. For EXCEPT ALL and INTERSECT ALL, both pins attempted the rule. Only the parent produced its projection rewrite.
Each deployment checks the JDK fingerprint, ordered artifact digests, caller classes and original class providers. The same compiled caller runs both sides in fresh JVMs.
